author: Cree Say
title: A SYMPHONY OF SECRETS The sins we hide series Book 4
text: course. Her internal clock was more accurate than NASA’s. I gently eased myself out of Jordan’s arms, careful not to wake him. He murmured something incoherent and reached for me instinctively, fingers brushing my waist before falling away when he realized I was gone. My heart squeezed. I slipped out of bed, grabbed my robe, and padded into the hallway where my two-year-old stood with her curls wild and her stuffed unicorn hanging from her hand like a hostage. “Good morning, baby,” I whispered, scooping her up. She cupped my cheeks dramatically. “You s’eepy, Mommy.” I smiled and kissed her forehead. “A little.” I carried her toward the kitchen, whisper-singing her morning song, trying to calm the storm still swirling in my chest. Last night changed us. Not officially. Not publicly. But privately, between sheets and shadows, something shifted. Ray giggled when I set her in her booster seat and handed her a banana. She kicked her little feet happily, humming to herself, blissfully unaware that her mother was having a quiet emotional crisis at 7:45 in the morning. I was cutting slices of strawberries when footsteps padded softly into the doorway. I didn’t have to turn to know it was him. Jordan leaned against the frame, hair a mess, shirt in his hand, looking like he walked straight out of a dream I shouldn’t be having but absolutely did. His eyes softened when he saw us,me at the counter, Ray in her seat, the morning sun spilling across the kitchen tiles. Something warm flickered through his expression, something that looked suspiciously like belonging. “Good morning,” he murmured, voice still rough with sleep. Ray squealed. “Jow-den!” She still couldn’t pronounce his name right. And he pretended he hated it but secretly adored it. He walked over and kissed her cheek, letting her grab his face with syrupy fingers without flinching. “Hey, bug,” he whispered, rubbing her back. “Missed me already?” She nodded so hard her curls bounced. “Uh-huh.” He smiled. And then he glanced at me. Not in a casual way. Not in a “we’re just friends” way. Not in a way I could ignore or pretend was something else. Heat bloomed under my skin. I hated that I blushed like a teenager around him. I hated it even more that he noticed every time. “You sleep okay?” he asked softly. “I did,” I replied, trying not to sound breathless. “You?” He gave me a small, crooked smile that made my stomach tighten. “Better than I have in a long time.” I swallowed hard. He stepped closer, stopping just behind me,close enough to feel his presence but far enough that he wasn’t assuming anything. It was his way of saying, I’m here. But you decide everything. And God… that made me want to kiss him again. Ray banged her spoon on the table. “Story! Mommy, story!” Her timing was perfect. Children have a sixth sense for interrupting tension. Jordan laughed softly and sat beside her, launching into a dramatic retelling of Goldilocks that involved unexpected plot twists, terrible accents, and exaggerated gestures. Ray was laughing so hard she nearly fell off her seat. Watching them like that,my daughter glowing, Jordan glowing, my home feeling warmer than it had in years,did something to me. A part of me whispered, This could be real. Another part whispered, You’re not ready. But when Jordan glanced at me over Ray’s head,eyes soft, smile small, expression vulnerable, I realized I was already halfway in, whether I wanted to be or not. After breakfast, Ray insisted on building a pillow fort in the living room. Jordan helped her, crawling on the floor, letting her order him around like a tiny general. He kept looking back at me as he worked,as if checking that I was okay, that last night hadn’t scared me off, that this morning wasn’t too much. And maybe that’s what undid me the most. He was gentle with me. He was patient with me. He was steady in all the places I wasn’t. Ray eventually fell asleep against his chest, tiny hands tangled in his shirt. Jordan just sat there, holding her, breathing in sync with her, looking like the moment was enough to rebuild him. Something in my chest tightened painfully. Because I knew I knew this was so much deeper than a casual kiss or a physical release or a temporary escape. This man was slipping into my life like he had always belonged there. And I was terrified of how good that felt. I sank onto the couch beside him, watching both of them. “Jordan,” I whispered. He looked over slowly, arm tightening protectively around Ray. “Yeah?” I hesitated, words stuck between fear and wanting. But then he reached for my hand,carefully, gently, like asking permission. I let him take it. And for the first time since everything in my life fell apart… I didn’t pull away. Twenty Seven Morning sunlight spills across my bedroom like warm honey, soft and lazy, as if the universe has decided to take its time today. For once, I want to follow its lead. No rushing, no running, no fear of being seen or photographed. Just a normal morning with my daughter,my safe place, my entire world,wrapped in a blanket beside me. Ray is awake before I even open my eyes. I feel her little fingers tapping my cheek, her voice trying to whisper but failing adorably. “Mama… mamaaaa… wake up, I hungry.” Her big green eyes blink at me with all the seriousness a two-year-old can muster, which isn’t much, because she bursts into giggles the moment I groan. I roll to my side and pull her on top of me, burying my face into her soft curls. She smells like baby shampoo and sleep, and I swear my entire heart becomes liquid. “Good morning, princess,” I mumble. She responds by patting my face again,roughly, because she still hasn’t figured out her strength,and announces, “Mama, I want pan-cates.” “Pancakes,” I correct softly, but she shakes her head like I’m the crazy one. “Pan-cates,” she repeats with conviction. I kiss her nose and give up. “Okay. Pan-cates it is.” Today was supposed to be a quiet day. That was the plan. No costumes. No crowds. No risks. Halloween has always felt like a neon sign flashing EXPOSED over my head, and now that I have a child whose existence the world is one whisper away from discovering, I’ve avoided it like the plague. The paparazzi haven't stopped circling like vultures since I moved to New York, and stepping outside in a costume-filled night felt like tempting fate. So the plan was simple: cartoons, blanket forts, snacks, and maybe a quiet dinner. Amy could go on her little sexcapade with her British boxer-slash new flavor of the month,God bless that chaotic woman,and Jordan and I… well, later tonight we’d probably end up in each other’s arms again, doing the things we’re still pretending don’t mean anything. We’re a complicated pair. Touching, kissing, exploring each other like we’re trying to learn the taste of new air, but still acting like titles ruin magic. He’s careful with me. Gentle. But there’s a fire beneath his gentleness that I pretend not to feel every time he presses me to a wall or whispers my name against my throat. Today was supposed to be simple. I lift Ray off me and slide out of bed as she toddles behind me toward the kitchen, dragging her unicorn plushie like she’s reenacting a dramatic breakup scene. I start the coffee. She climbs into her seat and bangs the table until I mix her batter. This is us. Our little bubble. Perfectly unremarkable. Perfectly safe. Except safe doesn't last long in this house. The moment I flip the second pancake, the front door opens without knocking. Ray gasps like someone just announced Christmas. “Jodannnn!” She squeals the name in her usual mispronunciation,Jodan, not Jordan,and instantly abandons her breakfast. I sigh because of course he has a key. I blame myself for that. One emergency turned into two, which turned into the casual normality of him walking into my home like it was his. And deep down, I don’t mind it. Actually, I love it far more than I should. He appears in the doorway, hair a bit messy, sweater sleeves pushed up, smile warm enough to melt glaciers. Ray barrels into his legs before he even finishes stepping in. He laughs and scoops her up, lifting her like she’s weightless. “Good morning, princess,” he murmurs, kissing her cheek loudly until she squeals. I watch them, my heart betraying me as usual, glowing painfully. I hate how easy this feels. How natural. How much it looks like a picture I was never supposed to want again. “You’re early,” I say, plating pancakes to distract myself. “We weren’t expecting you until ten.” “That’s because Amy texted me at six in the morning,” he says, rolling his eyes. “Something about getting ‘the sexy man’s opinion’ on Halloween costumes.” His tone carries mock suffering, but his grin gives him away. “And she said you’re refusing to celebrate today.” I stiffen immediately. He notices. He always does. “It’s not refusal,” I say quietly. “It’s safety.” He nods like he understands, then sets Ray in her chair. “Okay. But hear me out. What if we all stayed inside, dressed the kids up, let them have fun, maybe buy candy for a fake trick-or-treating around the apartment?” “That’s actually not a bad—” “—or,” he interrupts gently, his voice dipping low in that way that makes my spine react before my brain does, “you could trust me to keep you both safe outside. Just once. Just tonight.” I freeze, spatula mid-air. He moves closer, his voice soft enough that only I can hear him. “You don’t live in hiding anymore, Lys. You deserve to have fun too.” I hate how much those words hit me. I hate how much he wants me to live. But I hate most how much I want to say yes. Before I can respond, Amy bursts into the apartment like a tornado in leggings, holding Emeric on one hip and a red lace bag on the other. “ALRIGHT, PEOPLE!” she shouts dramatically. “It’s Halloween and nobody is sitting at home crying over their ex-husband tonight! Except maybe the ex-husband!” I glare. Jordan chuckles. Ray claps like this is entertainment. “I told you,” I groan. “I’m not—” “Oh shut it,” she snaps, tossing a costume onto my counter. “You’re Wonder Woman, Jordan’s Superman, I’m Catwoman, the kids are adorable, and we are going trick-or-treating whether you like it or not.” “I didn’t agree to—” “You will.” She points at Jordan. “Use your charm.” He doesn’t even hesitate. He walks behind me, close enough that his chest brushes my back, close enough that I can smell his cologne, close enough that I know he knows what he’s doing. His fingers graze the counter near mine, and his voice dips into something sinful. “We’ll keep you safe,” he murmurs, his breath warm at my ear. “I promise.” My entire body betrays me with a shiver. He feels it. Of course he feels it. Amy’s eyes go wide. “Oooooh he’s good.” I fan myself exaggeratedly in self-defense. “Absolutely not. Manipulation is not allowed before breakfast.” Jordan steps back with a smirk, smug and devastating. I try to resist. I do. But Ray tugs at my shirt, whispering, “Mama… I want pwetty dress.” And that’s it. That’s the end of me. Two hours later, I’m in a Wonder Woman costume, staring at myself in the mirror and wondering how the hell peer pressure still works on grown adults. Amy slinks out in her Catwoman suit, yelling “MEOW BITCHES!” like she’s possessed. Jordan emerges as Superman, and I swear my lungs forget their primary job. Ray twirls in her Princess Sofia gown, looking like an angel. Emeric proudly does the Paw Patrol salute. The whole scene is so cute it hurts. Despite every nerve in my body screaming anxiety, the kids’ excitement wins. We step outside into the cool October night, bundled in warmth, surrounded by lights and decorations. For the first thirty minutes, everything feels perfect. Children run past dressed as skeletons and witches. Parents laugh. Amy and I gossip. Jordan keeps a protective hand hovering near my back. Ray refuses to let go of his thumb. It feels like a family. It feels like something I shouldn’t want. Then it happens. A group of teenagers walking past slows down, squints at me, then at Ray, then at Jordan. My heart drops. One of the girls points, whispering rapidly, her phone already rising like a gun being cocked. “Oh my God… is that—” I grab Ray instinctively. Jordan steps forward immediately. “No pictures.” But it’s too late. One flash goes off. Then another. Then screaming. Then running. Someone yells my full name. Someone else says “whose baby.” Another shouts “Is that her new boyfriend?!” Everything spirals in seconds. Jordan grabs my waist. “We’re leaving. Now.” Security forms around us instantly, but the damage is done. Phones are up everywhere. Flashes blind me. Ray starts crying, terrified by the noise. My heart cracks open at the sound. Emeric cries next. Amy curses loudly. Jordan picks Ray up and shields her head as he pushes us toward the SUV waiting nearby. We pile in. Doors slam. The car launches forward. My breathing is shaky. My hands tremble uncontrollably. Jordan hands Ray to me and grabs my face gently, forcing my eyes to meet his. “You’re safe,” he whispers firmly. “Both of you are safe.” Ray sobs into my chest. I hold her so tightly I almost crush her. Amy tries to soothe Emeric, but even she looks shaken. My phone explodes with notifications. I don’t open them. I already know what’s happening. My name is trending. Photos of us are everywhere. The costume didn’t hide me. The night didn’t protect me. I walked into the world and it swallowed us whole. My throat tightens painfully. “Jordan… I shouldn’t have gone out. I shouldn’t have listened. I just put her in danger. I should have—” “Stop,” he says, voice rough with emotion. “This is not your fault. I promised to protect you and I will. I always will.” Something in me breaks open then,terror, relief, longing, everything tangled into one overwhelming spiral. I press my forehead to Ray’s hair and let myself breathe. Tonight was supposed to be simple. Instead, it changed everything. And deep down, I know this is only the beginning. Twenty Eight The moment the car doors slammed behind us, I felt my world fracture into a thousand pieces. Even with the SUV pulling into the garage, the flashes from the paparazzi followed us like relentless fireflies. They had positioned themselves perfectly, as though anticipating every movement, every breath. My stomach lurched, a cold, heavy weight settling like cement. Ray whimpered against me, clutching at my sweater with tiny fists, and I pressed her closer, trying to make myself smaller, invisible, untouchable. Jordan was already out, moving with controlled fury, his long legs cutting through the corridor between the flashes, body shielding Ray like she was a priceless gem. “Follow me,” he ordered, and I obeyed instinctively, heart hammering, fingers clutching the straps of my bag as if that would anchor me. Emeric clung to Amy, his sleepy little arms tightening around her neck, and I glimpsed Amy’s face,flushed but composed, already in publicist-mode. “You idiots,” she muttered under her breath as we passed, a low growl, fingers dancing over her phone, fingers flying faster than I could follow. I caught a glimpse of her screen: multiple browser tabs open, messages being sent, calls being made, tweets being flagged for deletion. She was fighting a war, and the battlefield was our lives. I wanted to run. I wanted to vanish. I wanted to press my palms to my eyes and make the world stop. Instead, I was forced forward, shoved into the hallway by security and Jordan’s firm grip. My phone vibrated relentlessly in my pocket, a chorus of doom. Notifications. Tweets. Instagram posts. Every single one containing my face, Ray’s face, my name splashed across headlines. Mystery Baby Revealed. Alyssa Spotted with Daughter: Is Isaiah the Father or Jordan? Secret Child Exposed. “Oh God,” I whispered, my voice breaking as tears welled in my eyes. “Oh God, Jordan… they’ll see… Isaiah…” My fingers trembled, reaching for my face, trying to shield it from the chaos. Jordan dropped to one knee beside me, catching my chin gently. His thumb brushed across my cheek, and his eyes held mine with a steady, unshakable force. “He won’t see anything yet,” he said, firm. “Amy’s on it. I’m on it. You are not alone. Ray is safe. Emeric is safe. You are safe. Nothing else matters right now.” But my mind raced uncontrollably. I imagined Isaiah scrolling through his phone, spotting Ray’s face, piecing together timelines, thinking, accusing. My chest tightened as if someone had wrapped a steel band around it. The panic rose like a tide I couldn’t fight. My knees buckled slightly, and I felt Jordan’s strong hands anchoring me, holding me upright against the tidal wave of dread. Amy’s voice cut sharply through the room. “We need to get control now!” she snapped, urgency layered over calm efficiency. “I’m flagging posts, contacting editors, calling social media managers. If these images don’t come down in the next twenty minutes, it’s going viral, and we have no control.” She barked orders into her phone, multitasking like a seasoned general, her other hand brushing Emeric’s hair back from his forehead. Jordan’s jaw tightened. He stepped into the fray, pulling out his phone and tapping into a network of contacts I barely even knew existed. “I’ve got three editors on standby.
